scripts.label: Tactic double attack played
scripts.text: The continuation creates two attacks at once. Watch how the two attacking pieces work together.

scripts.label: Tactic double attack allowed
scripts.text: This move allows two attacks at once in the continuation. Watch how the two attacking pieces work together.

scripts.label: Tactic double attack missed
scripts.text: The stronger continuation created two attacks at once. This move misses that chance to combine the threats.

scripts.label: Tactic deflection played
scripts.text: The continuation uses a deflection. A defender is drawn away, opening a tactical opportunity.

scripts.label: Tactic deflection allowed
scripts.text: This move allows a deflection in the continuation. An opposing move draws a defender away, opening a tactical opportunity.

scripts.label: Tactic deflection missed
scripts.text: The stronger continuation used a deflection. Drawing a defender away would open a tactical opportunity.

scripts.label: Tactic undefended capture played
scripts.text: The continuation captures an undefended piece. Keep an eye on loose pieces; they can offer a straightforward opportunity.

scripts.label: Tactic undefended capture missed
scripts.text: The stronger continuation captured an undefended piece. This move misses that chance, so give loose enemy pieces a careful look.

scripts.label: Tactic hanging piece allowed
scripts.text: This move allows the other side to capture an undefended piece in the continuation. Loose pieces deserve a careful look.

scripts.label: Cause opponent threat recognition
scripts.text: The opponent's previous move enabled this attack. This move leaves the threat unanswered, and the piece can be captured in the continuation.

scripts.label: Cause avoiding bad trades
scripts.text: This capture invites a recapture of a more valuable piece. Count both sides of the exchange before judging the first capture.

scripts.label: Positional development actual
scripts.text: This develops a minor piece from its original square. Notice its new place in the position.

scripts.label: Positional development alternative
scripts.text: The unplayed alternative would develop a minor piece from its original square. Notice where it would go.

scripts.label: Positional rook open actual
scripts.text: This leaves a rook on an open file. There are no pawns of either color on that file.

scripts.label: Positional rook open alternative
scripts.text: The unplayed alternative would leave a rook on an open file. That file would contain no pawns of either color.

scripts.label: Positional rook semi open actual
scripts.text: This leaves a rook on a semi-open file. There are no friendly pawns on that file, but at least one enemy pawn remains.

scripts.label: Positional rook semi open alternative
scripts.text: The unplayed alternative would leave a rook on a semi-open file, with no friendly pawns on that file but at least one enemy pawn.

scripts.label: Positional passed actual
scripts.text: This leaves a passed pawn: no enemy pawn is ahead on its file or either neighboring file.

scripts.label: Positional passed alternative
scripts.text: The unplayed alternative would leave a passed pawn, with no enemy pawn ahead on its file or either neighboring file.

scripts.label: Positional passer advance actual
scripts.text: This advances a pawn that was already passed. Keep its new square in view as you compare continuations.
